This one is worthy of weeping. It is not necessary to mourn the one dead, but the one dead having fallen away from blessedness and eternal life. In many ways, one can mourn himself having become lost in sins, if he perceives it. And he is blessed, the one mourning himself, having made himself worthy of mourning and having fallen from the blessed life, so that he may be comforted. …
comments.selected_reason: Explains who should be wept for according to the verse.
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: The word of Jeremiah about a righteous king raised up for David matches what was said of the one rising from the root of Jesse to rule the nations.
comments.comment: … Equally to the one rising from the root of Jesse as the ruler of all nations, what was fully spoken has the force of Jeremiah's word. For the same as 'rising from the root of Jesse the king of the nations' is: 'Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will raise up for David a righteous dawn, reigning as king, in whose days the people shall be saved' (Jer 23:5), he who confesses, being called 'Judah' with the voice of Hebrews, and the mind seeing God, being called 'Israel,' 'will tabernacle trusting,' according to that which is said by those who confess to the Lord of all: 'Have mercy on us, Lord, for in you we have trusted' (Isaiah 33:2). Concerning all who have stood thus boldly and manfully, it has been written: 'Blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord, and the Lord shall be his hope' (Ps 40:4).
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: God's word through Jeremiah shows that a prophet who misses the truth is speaking from his own heart and not from the Lord's mouth.
comments.comment: [On telling a true prophet from a false one:] Some such thing he says through Jeremiah’s voice: ‘I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God from far; if a human will be hidden in hidden places, will I not also see him? Do I not fill the heaven and the earth? says the Lord. Have I heard what the prophets speak—false things which the prophets prophesy in my name?’ (Jeremiah 23:23–25) Then through the middle having accused not a little those who have despised the divine laws, he gives the truth as a clear demonstration of both the things from God and not. For he said again: ‘The prophet in whom is his dream, and in whom is my word toward him, let him narrate my word upon truth.’ (Jeremiah 23:28) As if something should appear having missed the truth, it would show at once its begetter false-speaking, and speaking from his own heart, not from the Lord’s mouth, according as it has been written.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 6

comments.capsule: A captivity hangs over us for our sins, and the words of Scripture call us to repent, for God says He will repent of the evils He spoke of doing.
comments.comment: Because of our sins a captivity hangs over us too, and we are about to be handed over, if we do not repent, to Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians, so that the spiritual Babylonians may tear us. With these things hanging over us, the words of the prophets, the words of the Law, the words of the apostles, the words of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, speak to us about repentance and call us to a turning. If we hear, let us believe the one who said, 'I also will repent of all the evils which I spoke of doing to them.' (Jeremiah 26:3)
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria

comments.capsule: Christ is the new covenant promised through the prophet, and it is called new because it reshapes a person into the newness of a holy life, where Moses was a minister of shadow and type.
comments.comment: For our Lord Jesus Christ has been appointed by God the Father as a covenant for the race according to the flesh, I mean those of Israel, to whom God promised long ago through one of the prophets, saying: “Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will accomplish for the house of Israel and for the house of Judah a new covenant, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers” (Jeremiah 31:31-32). For the divine Moses was a minister of shadow and type, standing in the rank of a suppliant; but Christ, as Son and Lord, became the arbiter of a new covenant. I call it new because it reshapes man into the newness of a holy life, and through the Gospel way of life shows him to be an approved and true worshipper; for “God is Spirit,” it says, “and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth” (John 4:24).
comments.selected_reason: Says what is new about the new covenant in terms a reader can follow.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria

comments.capsule: God engraved a natural law on man in the beginning, and in the last times, the time of Christ's coming, He writes His laws on their hearts.
comments.comment: Taking the words in their universal sense and giving their meaning, we say that in the beginning the God of all fashioned man and engraved on him a natural law, training him toward the knowledge of evil and good. And this, I think, is what was said through the voice of John about the only-begotten Son of God: “He was the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world” (John 1:9). We understand that this also came about in the last times, I mean the times of his coming. For it is written: “In those days, says the Lord, putting my laws into their mind, I will also write them on their hearts” (Jeremiah 31:33; Hebrews 8:10).
comments.selected_reason: Explains the writing of the law on the heart as a fulfilment of what God did at creation.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria

comments.capsule: Christ writes God's laws on us in his own Spirit, so that we become his letter, which shows that he is God.
comments.comment: God said somewhere through one of the holy prophets: “In that time, says the Lord, I will put my laws into their mind, and I will write them on their hearts.” (Jeremiah 31:33) So we have become Christ’s letter — he writing on us what he wills not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God — not merely as a minister, but, so to speak, by his own working; for the Spirit is his own. Then how is he not God, who writes for us in his own Spirit the way of knowing God?
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On the True Faith, to the Princesses Arcadia and Marina

comments.capsule: God accused those who took back the servants they had set free, for He does not endure the types being set aside or the truth itself being treated as still in shadows.
comments.comment: … And since for the Jews having fallen back unto carelessness it did not seem very much to keep the things having been commanded, God was accusing those having chosen to do this. For it has been written that also ‘A word of the Lord became toward Jeremiah, saying: Thus said the Lord the God of Israel, saying: I covenanted a covenant toward your fathers on the day on which I took them out from Egypt’s land (Jeremiah 34:13) from a house of slavery saying: Whenever six years are filled, you will send out your Hebrew brother who will be sold to you, and he will work for you six years, and you will send him out free; and they did not hear me, and they did not lean their ear; and they turned today to do the straight before my eyes, to call a release each of his neighbor; and they completed a covenant according to my face in the house upon which my name has been called upon it; and you turned, and you profaned my covenant, to turn back each his servant, and each his maidservant, whom you sent out free in their soul, to be for you unto servants and maidservants.’ Do you see how he does not endure the types being set aside, or rather the truth itself being insolently treated as still in shadows?
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
comments.work: On Adoration and Worship in Spirit and Truth, Book 7

comments.capsule: Jeremiah's dark pit shows him as a type of Christ, who suffered much from the Jews.
comments.comment: … And specifically Pashhur also threw Jeremiah into the pit, being dark and without light—such as was also David’s cave in which he was hidden from Saul. And the two Laments could also be taken unto Christ, of whom Jeremiah was a type, having suffered so many things from Jews and at the end having been handed over to a tomb …
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria

comments.capsule: The enemies did nothing of themselves, for the Lord brought these evils on because the people sinned, as Nebuzaradan said and as all the prophets and Moses foretold.
comments.comment: Nothing, she [the speaker in Lamentations] says, did the enemies do from themselves; for it seemed good to God and has come to be. For which reason Nebuzaradan also was saying: “the Lord your God has spoken these evils unto this place, and the Lord has brought them on, because you sinned against him.” (Jeremiah 40:2-3) Everyone, then, who disbelieves the judgment will hear these words. All the prophets, then, were foretelling these things, and from ancient days Moses in Deuteronomy announced these things beforehand (Jeremiah 40:2–3).
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria

comments.capsule: Worship of heaven, the sun, the moon and the stars is not Jewish practice but a transgression of Judaism, and God reproaches the people through Jeremiah for sacrificing to the queen of heaven.
comments.comment: … though Celsus [the critic Origen is answering] thinks it a Jewish practice to worship heaven and the angels in it, such a practice is not Jewish but a transgression of Judaism, as is the worship of the sun, the moon and the stars, and of images too. You will find, at any rate, especially in Jeremiah, the word of God reproaching the Jewish people through the prophet for worshipping such things and for sacrificing “to the queen of heaven” (Jeremiah 44:17–19) and “to all the host of heaven” (Jeremiah 19:13).
comments.author: Origen of Alexandria

comments.capsule: Israel the wandering sheep was devoured by Assyria and then Babylon, the lions, who will be judged.
comments.comment: … That falling into the mouth of one eating signifies being defeated, as it is testified by many scriptures, and most especially by this: 'A wandering sheep of Israel, lions drove him out; the King of Assyria first devoured him, and later the King of Babylon devoured his bones.' (Jeremiah 50:17). In the same way, even if the lions were powerful, standing opposed through their ferocity as opposing forces, they shall endure judgment when Israel, having been trampled by them, is set free, having been allegorically called a sheep …
comments.author: Didymus the Blind

comments.capsule: Babylon is called the land of carved images for its many idols, or because its people were like idols.
comments.comment: … He [God] did this because sorcery abounded among them [the Babylonians] beyond measure and the swarm of their idols was past counting. Indeed, it has been called “the land of carved images” (Jeremiah 50:38), either because of the multitude of idols or because each of those who lived there was found to differ in no way from an idol, I mean in turning aside to error without check or restraint.
comments.selected_reason: Explains why Babylon is called the land of carved images.
comments.author: Cyril of Alexandria
